findings.title: Task 3 consumer list not written
findings.problem: Plan Task 3 Step 3 requires listing every consumer of last_event_at and fb.last_ts with its intended behavior in red-results.md; the file has no such list. The consumers (session_files_daily day window ~rollups.py:1225, get_session_cost_facts, get_users_last_active, session_purge._idle, the reader range) are only touched on afterwards as residual R9/R10.
findings.impact: The semantic shift of two stored columns that other code reads is not recorded against each reader, so a reviewer cannot confirm each consumer's behavior was intended; the plan marked it required.
findings.recommendation: Run grep -rn "last_event_at\|last_ts" src/ and add a table to red-results.md: consumer, file:line, behavior before and after, intended or not. Correct R9 in residual-risks.md: session_purge._idle also counts updated_at for owner-bound rows, so only legacy rows lose the reopen refresh.

findings.title: Default-list count loses its index-only scan
findings.problem: Arm 1 now filters on last_activity_day, which session_dims_active_shared_cov does not hold, so the ids-only sel and the count of arm 1 on the default Sessions list change from an Index Only Scan (63 buffers, 0 heap fetches) to a Bitmap Heap Scan on session_dims_active_started (1,586 heap blocks, 1,626 buffers) for a 7-day window of 100k sessions. It was recorded as residual R11 by the implementer, not accepted by the user, and measured only warm at 100k sessions. The storage guide still states an index-only count of arm (1) and quotes the earlier timings.
findings.impact: The hottest query (default Sessions list and count) reads about one heap page per 6-7 sessions in the window; at the guide's 10^6 sessions and a 30-day default window, and on a cold cache, this was the class of query that previously timed out, so the cost is unmeasured and may be material.
findings.recommendation: Human decision: (a) accept R11 for now, state it in the guide (fix the 'index-only count of arm (1)' sentence and the stale timings) and re-measure at scale before release; or (b) add last_activity_day to the INCLUDE list of session_dims_active_shared_cov in a migration (index rebuild on a large table, ops runbook entry); or (c) bound arm 1 without a new column read. The implementer cannot choose between (a) and (b) without knowing production volume and migration appetite.

findings.title: Later probe unbounded when the end is NULL
findings.problem: last_event_at is now NULL for a session with no real-work hook, so greatest(last_event_at, ended_at) can be NULL (ended_at also NULL when the summary lacks it and the raw fallback was not computed). The later probe then becomes ts > -infinity and ts <= infinity, so log_events and spans are scanned across all weekly partitions instead of one day.
findings.impact: Partition pruning is lost for the list, detail and duration queries on such sessions; the conditions are rare but introduced by this change (previously last_event_at was set by any dimension hook).
findings.recommendation: Bound the probes by the start when the end is NULL: use coalesce(end, start) in both bounds of later (guard sketch: ts > coalesce(coalesce(end, start), '-infinity') AND ts <= coalesce(coalesce(end, start) + interval '1 day', 'infinity')) and extend the existing probe unit test; add a live case for a session with usage rows and lifecycle hooks only.

findings.title: Duplicated end filter, metrics differ from plan
findings.problem: The plan (Task 3b) asks for one shared real-work definition used by the rollup and the reader and for lines metrics only. The diff adds _RAW_RANGE_SOURCES here, a separate real_work dict in reader._activity_range, and leaves _RAW_ACTIVITY_SOURCES; the rollup filters metric_points with ROLLUP_METRICS (lines plus active_time) while the reader admission check uses LINES_METRICS.
findings.impact: An active_time metric emitted at a reopen (for example while a /exit is typed) can extend the stored end, the exact failure being fixed, and the copies can drift apart on the next edit.
findings.recommendation: Use LINES_METRICS in _RAW_RANGE_SOURCES (update test_the_fallback_range_starts_at_any_record_and_ends_at_real_activity_only) and move the per-table end filters (hook types, log kind and built-in commands, span kind, lines metrics) into one small helper imported by both rollups.py and reader._activity_range; document that the admission raw check intentionally differs.

findings.title: End tolerance too loose; Review Focus tests missing
findings.problem: _END_HOOK_LAG is 60 s while D1's session.end is stamped 20 s after the last request, so counting a lifecycle hook seconds after the last activity would still pass. The plan's dedicated live tests for Review Focus 1, 2, 3 and 6 (lifecycle-only non-Claude session ending at its last usage, session.end seconds after the last tool, api_request before the first hook keeping the start, provisional summary with a cancelled SessionEnd keeping the full duration) do not exist; the reopen scenarios cover only the days-later case.
findings.impact: A regression that again lets session.end (or a lifecycle hook) shorten or extend the end by seconds, or that moves the start for an api_request-first session, passes the live file.
findings.recommendation: Tighten _expected_ms to about 2 s (the end is exactly the last D1 request in every seeded case), then add the four small live tests on the existing _Reopen helper; each runs derived and NULL-fact modes. Run the file on PG17 and PG14 again.
